note: 原创学习题，AI辅助编写，待用户审核；非考试真题。审核元数据不属于管理端请求字段，不可直接作为API请求或文章导入文件。未写数据库、未发布。

articles.title: A Notebook That Makes Room for Tomorrow

questions.stem: What makes Mina’s new notebook more useful than her old word lists?
options: It gives her a complete copy of each article she reads.
It helps her use words and see which ones need review.
It lets her add more new words without reviewing them.
It makes every evening’s study task exactly the same.
questions.explanation: 新笔记不仅把词与原句、个人例句联系起来，还帮助Mina回忆用法并发现需要复习的词。第5段指出，她不看中文也能解释例句，并清楚知道哪些词需要再次复习；这才是新方法的价值。

evidence.quote: She could also see exactly which words needed another review.

distractorNotes: A：她选取少量词和相关句子，没有完整抄写每篇文章。
C：新方法减少新词数量，并包含回忆和针对性复习。
D：她在疲惫时缩小任务，学习安排并非每天完全相同。

articles.title: The Question at the Back of the Classroom

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the source of Leo’s growing confidence?
options: He learns to answer classmates’ questions without preparation.
He proves that his first interpretation is usually correct.
He becomes able to read every paragraph without uncertainty.
He develops a way to examine questions using textual evidence.
questions.explanation: Leo的信心来自一套处理疑问的方法：先说明已理解的部分，再找出解释失效的位置，并依据文本比较其他可能。第5段直接说明，信心不是来自假装没有疑问；第6段也表明他愿意接受更强的证据。

evidence.quote: His confidence grew from having a way to investigate uncertainty, rather than from pretending uncertainty had disappeared.

distractorNotes: A：文章强调准备具体问题，没有说他无需准备就能回答同学。
B：他愿意根据更强证据改变看法，并非证明最初理解总是正确。
C：他仍有疑问，只是学会了如何调查和讨论。

questions.stem: Why did a volunteer suggest professional help for the damaged chair?
options: Its repair was beyond what the group could responsibly handle.
Its owner had not brought a question to the repair table.
The organizers allowed visitors to repair only electrical items.
The repair table required every damaged object to be replaced.
questions.explanation: 第4段说明，这把损坏的椅子超出了小组的能力范围，志愿者因此解释活动的边界，并建议找合适的专业人士。这里体现的是负责任地认识能力限制，而不是保证修好所有东西。

evidence.quote: Another visitor decided that a damaged chair was beyond the group's ability.

distractorNotes: B：原文没有说椅子主人未带问题，也未把这作为拒修理由。
C：现场也有缝纽扣和调整自行车座等活动，并非只修电器。
D：修理桌会尝试修理，未要求所有损坏物品都更换。

questions.stem: What does Nora learn about balancing screen use with other experiences?
options: A helpful routine should give every activity equal time.
A useful device should be put away on every journey home.
A flexible choice can give attention to what matters at the time.
A quiet walk should become a fixed daily study requirement.
questions.explanation: 最后一段明确解释，平衡不是把时间平均分配，而是判断何时设备有用、何时其他体验值得关注。Nora在雨天或赶时间时会调整安排，说明这种选择也应适应现实条件。

evidence.quote: It meant choosing when a device was useful and when another experience deserved attention.

distractorNotes: A：最后一段明确否定把每小时平均分成几份的理解。
B：她保留手机用于导航或重要电话，不是每次旅程都不能用。
D：她不希望散步成为让自己内疚的固定任务。

questions.stem: Which principle best explains the team’s decision about the planning app?
options: Positive user comments can replace checking permission information.
Permissions should be judged against actual needs and alternatives.
One limited trial can establish that an app will always be safe.
Useful shared lists require access to every saved phone contact.
questions.explanation: 团队先核对功能实际需要哪些信息，再查看说明、替代做法及账号删除规则，最后进行有限试用。第6段把这种做法总结为：检查功能需求、替代方案和解释是否清楚。因此应根据具体用途判断权限，而非直接给所有工具贴安全或不安全的标签。

evidence.quote: Before pressing "Allow," they had learned to ask what a feature needed, what alternatives existed, and whether the explanation was clear enough for the choice in front of them.

distractorNotes: A：第4段把用户评论视为个人经验，并与官方说明等信息比较。
C：第5段说明选择会随应用行为、设置或需求变化而调整，不是永久安全结论。
D：团队找到手动添加同学的方法，不必开放所有联系人。

articles.title: Choosing a Journey, Not Just a Vehicle
articles.titleZh: 选择一段行程，而不只是一辆车

questions.stem: In the final paragraph, what does “efficient” mean for the students’ design?
options: Making the whole journey work well for a particular need.
Making the vehicle move as fast as its equipment allows.
Using the newest machine available for every journey.
Using the least energy in a complete environmental comparison.
questions.explanation: 这里考查的是efficient在本文设计情境中的含义。最后一段将它解释为整段行程是否能满足具体需求；等待、出入口、无障碍信息等都属于考虑范围，不能仅按车辆速度或新旧程度判断。

evidence.quote: The word "efficient" now described whether a whole journey worked well for a particular need.

distractorNotes: B：第2段说明比较不能只看移动所花的时间。
C：更清晰的标识和路线图也可能改善行程，不一定要增加新机器。
D：第3段明确说缺少必要数据，因此没有完成全面环境比较。

articles.title: The Recipe with Three Different Endings

questions.stem: What does Mei’s experience suggest about a living tradition?
options: It needs one official history before people can share it.
It depends on serving exactly the same dish to everyone.
It becomes less meaningful whenever ingredients change.
It can remain familiar while adapting to people’s lives.
questions.explanation: 祖母的食谱本身就曾因食材和家庭人数而调整；这次家人又为不能吃某种食材的亲属准备替代份。结尾说明，变化没有使传统消失，熟悉的活动可以在适应真实生活的同时延续。

evidence.quote: The tradition had not disappeared because the recipe had changed.

distractorNotes: A：家人的故事没有组成唯一官方历史，也不妨碍分享食谱。
B：第3段强调欢迎家人比让每盘菜完全一样更重要。
C：结尾明确否定食谱变化就意味着传统消失。

articles.title: A Library Card and an Empty Chair
articles.titleZh: 一张借书卡与一把空椅子

questions.stem: Why does the library provide separate areas and visible signs?
options: To keep visitors without library cards out of the building.
To make every visitor take part in the conversation group.
To help different activities share the building with less disturbance.
To reserve the window seats for people preparing for examinations.
questions.explanation: 第3段先举出热闹交谈可能打扰备考者，再说明图书馆用不同区域和明显标识安排活动。这样做是为了兼顾不同使用者的需要，减少共享空间中的相互干扰。

evidence.quote: The library used separate areas and visible signs to explain where different activities belonged.

distractorNotes: A：第2段区分不同服务的规则，没有把所有无卡访客挡在门外。
B：会话小组允许发言、提问或只听，也不是每位访客都必须参加。
D：原文没有说靠窗座位只留给备考者。

articles.title: The Note That Helped the Next Shift
articles.titleZh: 帮助下一班同事的一份记录

questions.stem: Why does the team name a responsible person in the handoff note?
options: To show who can answer questions or make the next decision.
To identify who should be blamed if the project has problems.
To remove the need to confirm important changes directly.
To let the next shift avoid dealing with unresolved questions.
questions.explanation: 第5段明确区分责任人和追责：写名字是为了让下一班知道该找谁回答问题或作下一步决定；此人不在时还要列出替代联系人。这有助于工作衔接，而不是把所有沟通替换成文字。

evidence.quote: It showed who could answer a question or make the next decision.

distractorNotes: B：原文直接说明，点名不是为了出错时归咎于某人。
C：重要的截止时间或预期结果变化仍应直接确认。
D：记录让未决问题更清晰，便于继续处理，而非避开它们。

articles.title: A Meeting with Time to Think

questions.stem: What is the main lesson of the committee’s new meeting routine?
options: Better participation mainly depends on making everyone speak longer.
Useful participation depends on how people prepare and share ideas.
A successful meeting requires every proposal to receive agreement.
Written summaries can replace checking what members actually decided.
questions.explanation: 提前发议程、先安静写想法、两人讨论以及共同核对总结，为不同思考方式提供了参与机会。最后一段指出，参与不仅取决于谁说得最多，也取决于如何接收信息、准备回应及理解后续安排。

evidence.quote: It also depended on how people received information, prepared a response, and understood what would happen next.

distractorNotes: A：开头已经说明，仅要求大家多说并不能解决参与不均。
C：成员可以有理由地不同意提议，不要求每项提议都获一致赞成。
D：第5段要求成员核对总结是否准确反映实际决定。
